earlier_scan.source_named: Glottolog lists only Smith Stark 1994 (bibliographic survey); no grammar or phonology of Santa Catarina Albarradas Zapotec found.

sources.citation: ELAR catalogue search 'Albarradas'; archive.org advancedsearch 'Albarradas zapotec'; Crossref / Zenodo / DOAJ / CIESAS-repository queries 'Albarradas'; local AILLA and OLAC dumps
sources.note: No linguistic item on Santa Catarina Albarradas Zapotec found in any of these (hits are Santo Domingo Albarradas SIL items, mezcal/agave theses, Ecuadorian 'albarradas' ponds, herpetology).

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.x languoid record sant1448 (JSON) and SIL-Mexico website (familia zapoteca index; publicaciones por idioma; zapoteco-zas page)
sources.note: Glottolog: 0 descriptive refs, Glottolog's most extensive description 'a wordlist or less' (Smith Stark 1994). SIL-Mexico: no page and no publications for ztn; the zas page states that Santa Catarina Albarradas speaks 'otra variante'.

sources.citation: Valiñas Coalla, Leopoldo. 2020. Lenguas originarias y pueblos indígenas de México: familias y lenguas aisladas; grupos, lenguas y variantes. México: Academia Mexicana de la Lengua. (archive.org item valinas-2020-lenguas-originarias-y-pueblos-indigenas-de-mexico; pp. 351-354, no. 45 'La de Valles, del noreste.. dichsah o didxazá o.. dihidx bilyáhab').
sources.note: No phonology content: an encyclopedic catalogue (Diccionario de mexicanismos entries + INALI/Ethnologue variant lists). The ztn passage (scanned the text) gives municipalities, vitality ('lengua amenazada'), the ISO codes and that Santa Catarina's speech 'es diferente a la de Santo Domingo Albarradas'; the words tono/tonal/acento occur only 11 times in the whole 22,488-line book and never in the Zapotec de Valles section.

sources.citation: Beam de Azcona, Rosemary. 2016. Zapotecan languages. Oxford Research Encyclopedia of Linguistics (on-disk text in sibling dir asun1236); also Beam de Azcona 2018/2019 Southern Zapotec classification papers and Egland 1978 Sondeos de inteligibilidad (held by the project, sanv1242/xada1235)
sources.note: No mention of Albarradas at all (a full-text search for stress/accent = 0). Only the family-level remark that Zapotec shifted from Otomanguean final stress to stem-initial (usually penultimate) stress; not a statement about ztn.

sources.citation: Lewis, M. Paul, Gary F. Simons & Charles D. Fennig (eds.). 2016. Ethnologue: Languages of the World, 19th ed. Entry 'Zapotec, Santa Catarina Albarradas [ztn]'. Dallas: SIL International. (Internet Archive copy 2016-03-05)
sources.note: Nothing. Gives population (1,000, 1990), location (Santa Catarina Albarradas a.k.a. San Antonio Albarradas), '80% intelligibility of Santo Domingo Albarradas [zas]; Santo Domingo 52% of Santa Catarina. Differences in phonology and grammar.' No typology line; no grammar, dictionary or scripture listed under language development.

sources.citation: Marlett, Stephen A. (compiler). 2011 (March). Data sources. In: Cheryl A. Black, H. Andrew Black & Stephen A. Marlett (eds.), The Zapotec Grammar Files. SIL International (SIL Mexico electronic working papers WP001). 12 pp.
sources.note: No phonology content. It is SIL's own inventory of data sources per Zapotec ISO code for the cross-Zapotec Grammar e. SIL had no Santa Catarina Albarradas material feeding any grammar-files chapter as of 2011. Useful as a negative pointer only.

sources.citation: Marlett, Stephen A. (compiler). 2010 [February 2010 revision]. Basic vocabulary. In Cheryl A. Black, H. Andrew Black & Stephen A. Marlett (eds.), The Zapotec grammar files. SIL International (Mexico Branch) electronic working papers WP001i.
sources.note: Only one ztn form ('la') in the whole compilation, unmarked; the p. 3 penultimate-stress convention is vacuous here. Marks only / effectively no data.

sources.citation: Merrill, Elizabeth D. & Stephen A. Marlett. 2010 (February; PDF build 2018-04-06). Counting. In Cheryl A. Black, H. Andrew Black & Stephen A. Marlett (eds.), The Zapotec Grammar Files. SIL International (SIL Mexico electronic working papers WP001; mexico.sil.org/resources/archives/60866). 7 pp.
sources.note: No phonology content and no ztn data at all: the words stress/tone/accent do not occur; footnote 1 only refers the compiler to the separate 'Transcription Conventions' and 'Data Sources' files. The ztn row of the numeral table (the text) is empty, matching Marlett 2011 'Data sources' (PRIOR) in showing SIL had no Santa Catarina Albarradas material in the Grammar Files. Live sil.org copy is behind an automated-access block; downloaded through web.archive.org id_.

sources.citation: INALI. 2008 [print 2013]. Catalogo de las lenguas indigenas nacionales: variantes linguisticas de Mexico con sus autodenominaciones y referencias geoestadisticas, p. 191, variante <zapoteco de Valles, del noreste>.
sources.note: Nothing (locality catalog). Establishes identity: INALI lumps Santa Catarina Albarradas (mun. Villa Diaz Ordaz) with Santo Domingo / Santa Maria / San Miguel / San Lorenzo Albarradas as one variante 'zapoteco de Valles, del noreste' (dichsah / didxaza).

sources.citation: Kreikebaum, Wolfram. 1987. Fronting and related features in Santo Domingo Albarradas Zapotec. SIL-Mexico Workpapers 9: 33-71. (archive.org Rosetta extracts rosettaproject_zas_phon-1 / _detail-1; full scan in sibling dir sant1450)
sources.access_detail: a digital copy (available on request); access check: open copy online
sources.note: Describes Santo Domingo Albarradas Zapotec (zas, sant1450), NOT ztn; p. 33 says only 'The speech of Santa Catarina Albarradas is somewhat different.' For zas: 'Syllables are either stressed or unstressed. There are three tonemes.. In unstressed syllables there is neutralization of the rising and falling tones to a phonetic high pitch.' No stress-placement rule, and nothing on Santa Catarina.

sources.citation: Broadwell, George Aaron. 2015. The historical development of the progressive aspect in Central Zapotec. IJAL 81(2): 151-185.

sources.note: The only full phonological description of any Albarradas Zapotec; may contain comparative remarks on the Santa Catarina variety and is the nearest proxy (80%/52% intelligibility). Note it describes zas (sant1450), not ztn.

sources.citation: Egland, Steven (with Doris Bartholomew & Saul Cruz Ramos). 1978 [1983 2nd ed.]. La inteligibilidad interdialectal en Mexico: resultados de algunos sondeos. Mexico: ILV. (Zapotec section, Albarradas/Mitla test points)

sources.note: Source of the Ethnologue intelligibility figures for Santa Catarina Albarradas; confirms identity/affiliation (not expected to state stress). Scan held by the project (xada1235) has no text; not scanned here.
